fraud_veto_reason: Triple-trigger fraud veto: (1) 99.7% promoter pledging on 27.9% holding — one margin call away from control seizure and cascade sell-off; (2) Contingent liabilities ₹306 Cr exceed market cap ₹281 Cr — any crystallisation wipes out equity twice over; (3) Historical debtor days of 800–1600 days (yes, years, not months) for a decade is structurally inconsistent with real revenue — receivables that are never collected are not revenue. Combined with near-zero equity (₹4 Cr net), near-continuous losses for 11 of 12 years, and 88% revenue collapse from ₹955 Cr to ₹49 Cr, this company exhibits the hallmarks of a zombie entity sustained by balance-sheet manipulation and government-project billing with no cash conversion.
fcf_positive_years_note: FCF 'positive' in 7 of 12 years (2016–19, 2022–25) but MISLEADING — positivity driven by asset liquidation, working-capital release from collapsing business, and collecting old receivables on a shrinking base, NOT from operating profitability. EBITDA was negative in most of those same years.
debt_equity_note: Borrowings ₹90 Cr vs net equity ₹4 Cr (equity capital ₹176 Cr + reserves -₹172 Cr). Effective insolvency — negative reserves mean cumulative losses have eroded all shareholder capital.

reasoning: A2Z Infra Engineering is a textbook case of terminal financial distress with multiple overlapping fraud signals. The company peaked at ₹955 Cr revenue in FY2016 and has since collapsed to ₹49 Cr, destroying ₹904 Cr of shareholder equity through cumulative losses over 11 years. The core business never generated sustainable economics — interest costs alone exceeded operating profits in most years. The most damning signal is the debtor days history: receivables outstanding for 800–1600 days (2+ to 4+ years) are not receivables in any meaningful sense — they are phantom assets. Engineering companies can manipulate revenue by recognising project milestones without receiving cash, and the systematic inability to collect (1000+ day DSO for nearly a decade) strongly suggests billings that were either disputed, uncollectable, or fictitious. The 99.7% promoter pledging is a crisis in itself: promoters have borrowed against essentially 100% of their equity stake, which means they have already extracted maximum leverage. Any stock price decline triggers margin calls, which forces lender selling, which drives the price down further — a death spiral with no floor. The contingent liabilities of ₹306 Cr exceeding market cap is an existential threat: bank guarantees on failed or disputed infrastructure projects, if called, would immediately exceed the entire market capitalisation of the company. The near-zero book value (₹0.26/share, net equity ₹4 Cr) means the market is paying ₹281 Cr for a business with ₹4 Cr of net assets and ₹306 Cr of contingent claims — economically irrational except as speculation. While FCF appears positive in some recent years, this reflects asset liquidation and old receivable collection on a rapidly shrinking base, not operating health. The FY2026 FCF turned -₹33 Cr as the business tries to re-grow, indicating the positive FCF phase was winding-down activity, not sustainable operations. FRAUD VETO INVOKED on three independent grounds: (1) contingent liabilities exceed market cap, (2) 99.7% promoter pledging, (3) multi-year revenue with no cash conversion. This stock is a value trap with existential financial risks. Score: 1/10.
